title: Phonon down-conversion by normal metals for superconducting devices
abstract: Thanks to low dissipation, superconducting devices are promising for a number of applications, such as detectors and implementations of quantum computation. However, their working can be adversely impacted by quasiparticles, which is why so-called quasiparticle poisoning mechanisms and their mitigation are under intense investigation. Here we focus on one poisoning mechanism, namely pair-breaking phonons, and its mitigation through down-conversion by a normal-metal film - the process in which scattering of high-energy phonons by electrons lowers the energy of the former below the pair-breaking threshold. To study the down-conversion, we introduce a model based on kinetic equations, which we solve both analytically (approximately) and numerically in the steady state. We use the solution the estimate a properly-defined down-conversion efficiency which depends on material parameters (such as the strength of electron-phonon interaction and the phonon transmission coefficient at interfaces) and film and substrate thicknesses. Interestingly, we find that the efficiency is nearly optimal over a finite range of metal thicknesses, with the minimum near-optimal thickness being typically of the order of a micron.
summary: This paper models how high-energy phonons, which can damage superconducting qubits, are suppressed through a process called down-conversion within an adjacent normal metal film. By solving coupled kinetic equations for electron and phonon populations, the authors determine that this mitigation mechanism is most effective when the normal metal layer has a thickness near one micron.
main_problem: The primary goal is mitigating quasiparticle poisoning in superconducting devices caused by pair-breaking phonons.
main_result: Phonon down-conversion efficiency, which reduces the damaging high-energy phonons, is found to be nearly optimal over a finite range of normal metal thicknesses, typically around one micron.
method: The study employs kinetic equation modeling solved in the steady state to track phonon and electron distributions. Analytical and numerical solutions are used to calculate the down-conversion efficiency based on material parameters.
model_or_system: The system involves a superconducting device coupled via a normal metal film to a substrate, where high-energy phonons scatter off electrons, transferring energy and lowering the phonon energy below the pair-breaking threshold.
key_observables: Down-conversion efficiency ($R_{qp}$ or $R_\lambda$), electron distribution function ($f(E)$), and phonon distribution functions ($n(\Omega)$, $n_s(\Omega)$).
important_parameters: Material parameters like electron-phonon interaction strength, phonon transmission coefficients ($	au_{sm}, 	au_{ms}$), film thickness ($d_m$), and substrate thickness ($d_s$).
main_assumptions: Approximations include neglecting spatial gradients, assuming particle–hole symmetry for electrons, using the Debye model for phonons (ignoring anharmonic effects), and neglecting electron-electron scattering.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the physical setup (superconducting qubit chip with normal metal islands) and show the steady-state evolution of electron and phonon distributions under various injection conditions.
paper_structure: The paper develops a kinetic equation model for coupled phonon/electron dynamics, solves for the steady state using limiting cases (no-metal, perfect absorption), derives explicit formulas for down-conversion efficiency via asymptotic analysis, and discusses parameter dependence on geometry.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses energy dissipation mechanisms in superconducting circuits, which is crucial for maintaining quantum coherence. The detailed kinetic modeling of phonon relaxation provides insights into open quantum system dynamics driven by the environment (phonons).

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic depiction of a superconducting qubit chip with normal metal islands on the backside. The physical pro- cesses included in the kinetic equations are all represented: phonon escape to the sample holder (lifetime τes); phonon transmission from substrate to metal (τsm) and from metal to substrate (τms); electron-phonon interaction (τel and τph). Phonon transmission at the substrate-superconductor inter- face (τsS and τSs) has to be accounted for in the calculation of the down-conversion efficiency.

FIG. 3. Down-conversion efficiency Rqp, Eq. (46), vs. nor- malized ‘effective temperature’ ˜E/∆for a 100 nm Al film (∆= 0.18 meV, λ ≃0.44) and three values of injection en- ergy, see legend. The solid lines are obtained from numerics, the dashed lines using Eq. (53) (the discrepancy is due to λ < 0.5 being outside the validity regime of analytical ap- proximations). In the shaded region, ˜E/∆> 1, energetic quasiparticles in the superconductor can emit phonons and limit the efficiency; we exclude this regime from our analysis.
